title: Split a tablet in a splitter: seat it in the V-cradle, then close the blade on it
instruction: Cut the tablet in half with the tablet splitter.
context: Done by: pharmacy technicians and nursing assistants splitting half-dose tablets (O*NET 29-2052, 31-1131). A tablet cut off centre gives two unequal doses; the splitter's V centres a round tablet under the blade once it touches both sides. The instruction does not mention the V. Unlike TK-UQBJUF (card lined up to a printed mark on a guillotine) and TK-UJB387 (a block pressed into a corner stop), the task tests using a locating feature, and never closing the blade before the part is located.
setup: Positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: 'out' is away from the arms, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top. Tablet splitter (loose but heavy, 2 kg, standing on the table), described in its own frame: 'ahead' is along its blade line from the lid's pivot toward the robot. A light blue plastic base plate 165 mm long, 130 mm wide and 8 mm thick, running from 10 mm behind the pivot to 155 mm ahead of it. On it, two dark grey plastic walls (1.5 kg each, resting on the plate) 7 mm tall, 5 mm thick and 49.5 mm long form a V pointing away from the robot: their inner faces meet at an apex on the blade line 15 mm ahead of the pivot, each at 45 degrees to the blade line, so the V is 70 mm wide at its mouth, 50 mm ahead of the pivot. The lid is hinged on a white pin 26 mm above the table (two white posts 45 mm either side of the blade line). It is a blue plastic frame 80 mm wide and 77 mm long (rails 8 mm wide, open in the middle) with a dark steel blade bar 4 mm wide and 6 mm deep under its centre line, from 12 to 75 mm ahead of the pin. Closed flat, the bar lies along the blade line with its underside 10 mm above the plate; with nothing under it the lid tips a little further, until the bar's tip nearly reaches the plate. It starts standing open, leaning back 8.6 degrees onto its stop. Tablet (loose, 20 g, rigid): a white disc 30 mm across and 10 mm thick, lying flat on the plate. Lot A: the pivot 305 mm out on the midline, the blade line pointing straight out; the tablet 115 mm ahead of the pivot and 32 mm to the left of the blade line. Lot B: the pivot 305 mm out and 80 mm right of the midline, the splitter turned 20 degrees so the V's point turns toward the robot's left; the tablet 115 mm ahead and 32 mm to the right of the blade line. Lot C: the pivot 305 mm out and 80 mm left, turned 20 degrees the other way; the tablet 65 mm ahead of the pivot on the blade line, its front edge at the V's mouth, under the blade. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, read at the end with no gripper or finger within 5 mm of the tablet or the lid, the tablet still and the lid not moving. The blade line is the V's centre line. Seated: the tablet lies flat on the plate (tilted at most 10 degrees, lowest point within 1 mm of the plate) touching both walls (the gap from its edge to each wall at most 1 mm, which puts its centre within 0.7 mm of the blade line). Blade down: the bar's underside within 1 mm of the tablet's top. 1.0: seated with the blade down on it. 0.5: seated, blade not down. 0 otherwise. 0 for the rest of the trial if at any point the bar comes down to within 1 mm of the tablet's top while, seen from above, the tablet is under the bar with a gap of more than 1.5 mm to either wall (an off-centre cut), or if the splitter is pushed more than 3 mm or turned more than 2 degrees, or a wall more than 2 mm, from its place. Possible scores 0, 0.5, 1.0. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Lift the lid and stand it back on its stop. Set the splitter, its two walls and the tablet for the lot (positions and turn in setup). Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: Nothing is cut: the task scores where the blade comes to rest on the tablet. The tablet is about three times a real tablet's size so the top camera sees it, and the splitter is scaled to match. Real splitters have a sprung lid and fixed walls; here the rigid lid falls on a damped hinge, and the splitter and its walls are heavy loose parts only so the lots can move them. Tablet friction is about 0.2 on the plate and 0.6 on the walls.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
